surfaces.part: ground field (seamless earth tiles, full 96x80 area)

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless terrain texture: mottled brown earth with tonal patches, cracks and pebbles, filling every row at a constant width of 96 px. There is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no vertical face. The column scans show only irregular tonal changes (L about 60-118) with no structured band edges. It is a flat ground surface with no front face, which is expected for terrain tiles, so it reads as a flat top-down field.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts: the candidate has 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, so it is between the two references. Near-flat coverage is 1%, with no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so any dark tone is tinted brown and there is no sticker outline. By eye, the soil is a mottled brown field with a light-to-dark ramp of about 5 steps, dark speckle pebbles and crack-like streaks. It is a plausible dusty earth. However, the patches read as uniform noise rather than the clustered, hand-placed texture of the Beodeul grass tufts and individually shaded paving stones. The raw palette is only 5 colours, so the texture is fairly even and repetitive and less structured than the references. The long cracks and tonal patches described in the brief are weak and barely visible at this scale. Overall it is close to the reference but slightly lower in structured density and craft, and the cracks and pebbles are not clearly readable across tile borders.
